newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament turns down privatisation head.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament turns down privatisation head.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament rejected President Leonid Kuchma's candidate for head of the State Property Fund (FDM) on Wednesday.
Volodymyr Lanovy, acting privatisation chief since Kuchma appointed him last month, would have required 226 votes in his favour but received only 148, with 108 opposed.
Speaker Olexander Moroz said Lanovy would continue as acting chief of the state privatisation agency, previously headed by Yuri Yekhanurov who was appointed Economy Minister in February.
Parliament's economic policy committee must resolve whether Lanovy's candidacy should be renewed or whether a new candidate should be put forward, Moroz added.
One deputy said reformist deputies opposed Lanovy because they did not view him as a reformer while communist deputies were against him because they though him too reformist.

In his short term in office Lanovy, also head of the Kiev International Stock Exchange, promised to finish privatising Ukraine's medium- and large-scale enterprises and to increase share issues on Ukrainian stock markets.
